body: Bushido Blade 2 is Lightweight's PlayStation weapon-fighting game, first released in Japan on 12 March 1998. Rival schools of assassins pursue their own goals through confrontations where a well-placed strike can decide the outcome abruptly. The player chooses a fighter and weapon, then judges distance, stance and the opponent's movement instead of simply wearing down a long health bar. The sequel gives the Narukagami and Shainto schools a more structured conflict, keeping the original's interest in the danger carried by a single blade while rearranging the journey around it.

Swords and polearms give the fighters different possibilities at close and middle distance. Moving forward is a commitment because an opponent can answer before a combination has properly begun. The sequel adds dual-sword attacks and changes several of the first game's systems, asking returning players to adjust familiar habits. Support characters appear during the story, and completing a stage with one can unlock that fighter elsewhere. The roster therefore grows through participation in the campaign, making another encounter an opportunity to learn a different relationship between reach, movement and risk.

The original's large connected setting gives way to a sequence of maps, often placing groups of lesser opponents before a rival from the other school. This creates a more clearly staged progression while retaining the threat of decisive weapon contact. Kunihiko Nakata directed the sequel, with Ryuji Sasai composing its music. The North American release followed in October 1998. Bushido Blade 2 remains unusual among its contemporaries because the exchange is always fragile: the player has to respect the next attack even before a long contest has had time to develop.
